question_text: Which vehicle do firefighters use to put out fires?
explanation: Firefighters ride in a fire engine to get to fires quickly. It carries water and a long hose to put out the flames.

question_text: How many wheels does a bicycle have?
explanation: A bicycle has two wheels. You pedal with your feet to make it go, and you need to balance to stay up!

question_text: Which vehicle flies high up in the sky and carries lots of people?
explanation: An airplane has wings and very strong engines that let it fly through the sky. It can carry hundreds of people at once!

question_text: What color is a school bus?
explanation: School buses are painted bright yellow so drivers can see them easily and keep children safe on the road.

question_text: Which vehicle travels on train tracks?
explanation: A train has metal wheels that roll along rails called train tracks. Trains can carry many people or heavy loads.

question_text: Which vehicle travels on water?
explanation: A boat floats on water and can travel across lakes, rivers, and oceans. Some boats use sails, and others use engines.

question_text: What sound does a car horn make?
explanation: Cars have a horn that goes beep-beep to warn other drivers or people nearby. It helps keep everyone safe.

question_text: Which vehicle do doctors and nurses ride in to help sick people fast?
explanation: An ambulance rushes sick or hurt people to the hospital very quickly. It has a loud siren so other cars move out of the way.

question_text: How many wheels does a car have?
explanation: A car has four wheels — two in the front and two in the back. The wheels spin to move the car forward.

question_text: Which vehicle spins its blades on top to fly through the air?
explanation: A helicopter has spinning blades on top called a rotor. The spinning blades lift the helicopter straight up into the air.

question_text: Which vehicle travels under the water?
explanation: A submarine can dive deep under the ocean. It has tanks that fill with water to help it sink down and go up again.

question_text: Which vehicle is used on a farm to pull heavy loads?
explanation: A tractor is a big, powerful vehicle used on farms. Farmers use it to plow fields and carry heavy loads.

question_text: What goes up into space?
explanation: A rocket shoots fire from its bottom and blasts off into space. Rockets carry astronauts to the space station and beyond.

question_text: A hot-air balloon floats in the ___.
explanation: A hot-air balloon floats in the sky because hot air inside the big bag is lighter than the cool air outside.

question_text: What color is a fire engine usually?
explanation: Fire engines are almost always painted bright red. The bold color helps people notice them coming from far away.

question_text: Which vehicle carries people across the sea on a very long trip?
explanation: A large ship can sail across the ocean carrying hundreds of people. Big ships are sometimes called ocean liners.

question_text: A police car makes a loud noise to warn people. What is that noise called?
explanation: A police car has a siren that makes a loud wailing sound. The siren tells other drivers to move aside quickly.

question_text: Which of these vehicles only has two wheels and an engine?
explanation: A motorcycle has two wheels and a strong engine. The rider sits on top and steers with handlebars.

question_text: What sound does a train make?
explanation: Old steam trains made a loud 'choo choo' sound when steam puffed out. That is why children often call them choo-choo trains!

question_text: Which vehicle uses wind to move across the water?
explanation: A sailboat has a big sail that catches the wind. When the wind blows into the sail, it pushes the boat across the water.

question_text: A truck is used to carry ___ from place to place.
explanation: Trucks have a big space at the back to carry heavy loads like food, furniture, or boxes from one place to another.

question_text: Which of these vehicles can you pedal with your feet?
explanation: You pedal a bicycle by pushing the pedals with your feet. The pedals turn the wheels and move you forward.

question_text: Which vehicle would you take to travel from one country to another very quickly?
explanation: An airplane can fly very fast and travel thousands of miles in just a few hours. It is the quickest way to travel far.

question_text: A scooter is a small vehicle you can ride on the ___.
explanation: A scooter is ridden on roads or paths. You can stand on it and push with one foot, or use a small engine to go.

question_text: How many wheels does a tricycle have?
explanation: A tricycle has three wheels — one at the front and two at the back. The extra wheel makes it easy to balance.

question_text: Which vehicle is long and carries many passengers on city streets?
explanation: A bus is a long vehicle that can carry many people at once. City buses stop at many places to let people on and off.

question_text: What does an ambulance carry?
explanation: An ambulance carries sick or injured people to the hospital. It has medical equipment inside to help people feel better on the way.

question_text: Which vehicle can pick up garbage and take it away?
explanation: A garbage truck drives down streets to pick up rubbish from bins. It has a big container that squishes the garbage inside.

question_text: What do you call the person who drives a train?
explanation: The person who drives a train is called a train driver. They sit at the front and control how fast the train goes.

question_text: What do you call the person who flies an airplane?
explanation: The person who flies an airplane is called a pilot. Pilots train for many years to learn how to safely fly a plane.

question_text: Which vehicle can you use to go down a snowy hill?
explanation: A sled slides down snowy hills on smooth runners. You sit on top and zoom down the hill — it is very fun!

question_text: Which vehicle has a very long body made of many parts joined together?
explanation: A train has many carriages joined together in a long line. The engine at the front pulls all the carriages along the track.

question_text: What kind of road does a car travel on?
explanation: Cars drive on paved roads made of tarmac or concrete. Roads connect towns and cities so people can travel between them.

question_text: Which vehicle would you see in the sky at night with flashing lights?
explanation: Airplanes have flashing lights on their wings and tail so other pilots can see them in the dark sky at night.

question_text: What do astronauts travel in to reach outer space?
explanation: Astronauts travel in a rocket to reach outer space. The rocket burns huge amounts of fuel to blast away from Earth.

question_text: Which vehicle has two wheels, pedals, and no engine?
explanation: A bicycle has two wheels and pedals but no engine. You use your own leg power to make it move.

question_text: What is a canoe?
explanation: A canoe is a small, narrow boat that you move through water with a paddle. You sit inside and use the paddle to steer.

question_text: Which of these vehicles would you use to travel on a lake?
explanation: A kayak is a small boat that you paddle across a lake or river. You sit low in the water and use a double-ended paddle.

question_text: Which vehicle is used to carry lots of heavy things like sand or rocks?
explanation: A dump truck has a huge open container at the back that can tip up to empty heavy loads like sand, rocks, or dirt.

question_text: A police car is used to help keep people ___.
explanation: Police officers drive police cars to patrol streets and keep people safe. Their cars are fast and easy to spot.

question_text: Which of these flies through the air with spinning blades but can hover in one spot?
explanation: A helicopter can hover in one spot because its spinning blades keep it up. That makes it great for rescues!

question_text: What is the front part of a train called?
explanation: The front part of a train is called the engine or locomotive. It is the most powerful part and pulls the rest of the train.

question_text: Which vehicle carries people and their cars across a river or bay?
explanation: A ferry is a big flat boat that carries people and even cars across a stretch of water. Cars drive on, and the ferry sails across.

question_text: What color is a typical taxi cab?
explanation: In many cities, taxis are painted bright yellow. The color makes them easy to spot when you need a ride.

question_text: Which vehicle is very long, hauls heavy cargo, and drives on highways?
explanation: A semi-truck is a very long, powerful truck that can pull a huge trailer. It is used to move cargo over long distances.

question_text: What does a submarine use to see underwater?
explanation: A submarine uses a periscope — a long tube with mirrors — to look above the water while still being hidden below.

question_text: Which of these vehicles is the largest?
explanation: A ship is much larger than scooters, bicycles, or motorcycles. Some ships are as long as several city blocks!

question_text: Where does an airplane land?
explanation: Airplanes land at an airport on a long, flat strip of road called a runway. Airports have special areas for passengers too.

question_text: What makes a car go?
explanation: Most cars have an engine that burns fuel like petrol to make power. That power turns the wheels and moves the car.

question_text: A bulldozer is used on a building site to ___.
options: Push and move large amounts of dirt
explanation: A bulldozer has a big metal blade at the front. It pushes heavy dirt or rubble out of the way to clear space for building.

question_text: What part of a car do you turn to make it go left or right?
explanation: The steering wheel is in front of the driver. Turning it makes the car's front wheels point left or right.

question_text: What lights help drivers see at night?
explanation: Headlights are the bright white lights at the front of a car. They light up the road so the driver can see.

question_text: What should every kid wear when riding in a car?
explanation: A seat belt holds you safely in your seat. It keeps you from getting hurt if the car has to stop suddenly.

question_text: What do you wear on your head when riding a bike?
explanation: A bike helmet protects your head if you fall. Always buckle the strap so it stays on tight.

question_text: What is the person called who drives a boat?
explanation: The captain is in charge of the boat. They steer it and decide where it goes.

question_text: Where does a train stop to let people get on and off?
explanation: A train station has long platforms next to the tracks. People wait there for the train to arrive.

question_text: Where do airplanes take off and land?
explanation: An airport has long flat runways and a big building called a terminal. That's where planes pick up passengers.

question_text: What does a sailboat use to catch the wind?
explanation: A sail is a big piece of cloth on top of the boat. When the wind blows on it, the boat moves through the water.

question_text: What heavy thing keeps a boat in place when it stops?
explanation: An anchor is a heavy metal hook. It drops to the bottom of the water and stops the boat from floating away.

question_text: What do you use to move a canoe through the water?
explanation: A paddle has a flat end you push through the water. Each push moves the canoe forward.

question_text: Which truck takes broken cars to a garage?
explanation: A tow truck has a strong hook or platform on the back. It can pull a car that won't drive on its own.

question_text: Which truck brings letters and packages to your house?
explanation: Mail trucks bring letters and packages from the post office to homes. Mail carriers drive them every day.

question_text: Which vehicle plays music as it drives around selling treats?
explanation: An ice cream truck plays a happy song so kids know it's coming. It sells frozen treats from a window.

question_text: How many wheels does a skateboard have?
explanation: A skateboard has four small wheels — two at the front and two at the back. You push with one foot to go.

question_text: What has just one wheel and is pushed by hand to move dirt or rocks?
explanation: A wheelbarrow has just one wheel at the front and two handles at the back. Gardeners use it to carry things around.

question_text: What helps a person move around when their legs can't walk?
explanation: A wheelchair has two big wheels you can push with your hands. It lets people get around without walking.

question_text: What is the round black part of a wheel that touches the road?
explanation: A tire is the rubber ring around the outside of a wheel. It grips the road so the car doesn't slip.

question_text: What stops a bike from rolling?
explanation: Brakes squeeze the wheels so they stop spinning. You squeeze the handles to make them work.

question_text: Where do cars get fuel to run?
explanation: A gas station has pumps that fill a car's tank with fuel. Without fuel, most cars can't go anywhere.

question_text: What does an electric car use instead of gasoline?
explanation: An electric car has a big battery inside that stores power. You plug it in to charge, like a giant phone.

question_text: Which truck spins a big drum to mix concrete?
explanation: A cement mixer has a big drum that turns slowly. Spinning keeps the wet concrete from getting hard before it's poured.

question_text: Which big machine has a tall arm that lifts heavy things on building sites?
explanation: A crane has a long arm called a boom. It lifts steel beams and heavy loads up to the tops of buildings.

question_text: Which machine has a big arm with a bucket that digs holes in the ground?
explanation: An excavator has a big arm with a bucket on the end. It scoops dirt out of the ground to dig holes.

question_text: What do you push your baby in?
explanation: A stroller has wheels and a comfy seat with straps. Parents push it so babies can ride along on walks.

question_text: Who delivers letters and packages to homes?
explanation: A mail carrier brings letters to every house on their route. They drive a mail truck and walk up to each door.

question_text: What red sign with eight sides tells cars to stop?
explanation: A stop sign is red with eight sides. Cars must come to a complete stop before they can go again.

question_text: What color light tells cars they can go?
explanation: A green traffic light means it is safe to go. Red means stop and yellow means slow down.

question_text: What color light tells cars to stop?
explanation: A red traffic light means stop. Cars must wait until it turns green before they go.

question_text: What painted lines on the road show kids where to cross?
explanation: A crosswalk is a row of white stripes painted across the road. It shows drivers where people will be walking.

question_text: What should you wear in case you fall in the water from a boat?
explanation: A life jacket is filled with foam that floats. It keeps your head above the water until you can be rescued.

question_text: Which vehicle has a long platform you stand on with two small wheels and tall handlebars?
explanation: A scooter has two wheels and tall handlebars. You stand with one foot on the platform and push with the other.

question_text: What do firefighters slide down to get to their truck quickly?
explanation: A fire pole goes from the upstairs room down to the trucks. Firefighters can slide down it much faster than running.

question_text: Which big truck has a long ladder that reaches very high?
explanation: Some fire trucks have a long ladder folded on top. It can stretch up to high windows so firefighters can rescue people.

question_text: What do many people share to travel around a city?
explanation: A city bus picks up many people at bus stops. Sharing one bus is faster and easier than many cars on the road.

question_text: What is the small room at the front of a plane where the pilots sit?
explanation: The cockpit is the pilots' workspace at the front of the plane. It has all the controls and screens they need to fly.

question_text: Where do your suitcases go when you ride in a car on a trip?
explanation: The trunk is the storage area at the back of a car. You can fit suitcases, groceries, and other things inside.

question_text: What kind of car has an open box in the back for carrying things?
explanation: A pickup truck has a passenger seat in front and an open box in the back. The open box is good for carrying tools or boxes.

question_text: What car has a roof that can fold down so you ride in the open air?
explanation: A convertible has a roof that folds back. With it down, you can feel the wind in your hair as you drive.

question_text: Which vehicle has skis at the front and zooms across snow?
explanation: A snowmobile has skis at the front and a track on the back. It zooms across snowy fields and frozen lakes.

question_text: What part of a car makes the loud beep sound?
explanation: The horn is a button on the steering wheel. Drivers honk it to warn other people on the road.

question_text: What machine cuts wheat and other crops on a farm?
explanation: A combine harvester has a wide front that cuts plants. It separates the seeds from the stalks all at the same time.

question_text: What machine turns over the soil on a farm so seeds can be planted?
explanation: A plow has sharp blades that dig into the dirt. Pulling it through a field flips the soil so it's ready for planting.

question_text: What are the helicopter's spinning blades on top called?
explanation: A helicopter's spinning blades on top are called rotors. They push air down to lift the helicopter up.

question_text: What do airplanes need on their sides to stay up in the air?
explanation: Wings stick out from both sides of the plane. The shape of the wings creates lift, which holds the plane up in the sky.

question_text: What do you push around a store to carry your groceries?
explanation: A shopping cart has four wheels and a deep basket. You push it down the aisles and put your groceries inside.

question_text: What kind of small boat is moved with two oars?
explanation: A rowboat is small enough for one or two people. The rower sits facing backward and pulls on two long oars.

question_text: Which tiny boat is small but strong enough to push big ships through harbors?
explanation: A tugboat is small but very powerful. It pushes or pulls big ships into and out of crowded harbors.

question_text: Which giant boat takes thousands of people on long ocean vacations?
explanation: A cruise ship is like a floating hotel with pools, restaurants, and rooms. It carries thousands of passengers around the world.

question_text: What very fast little boat skips across the top of the water?
explanation: A speedboat has a powerful engine and a small light body. It goes so fast it almost flies above the water.

question_text: What small water vehicle do you ride like a motorcycle on a lake?
explanation: A jet ski has handlebars like a motorcycle. You sit or stand on it and shoot across the water using a powerful jet.

question_text: What ride at a fair has carriages on a track that go up and down hills very fast?
explanation: A roller coaster has cars on a winding track. It climbs slowly to the top, then zooms down with twists and loops.

question_text: What giant wheel ride lifts you slowly into the air for a great view?
explanation: A Ferris wheel is a huge wheel with seats on the edge. It spins slowly so you can see far in every direction.

question_text: What kind of tiny car bumps into others for fun at amusement parks?
explanation: Bumper cars have soft rubber bumpers all around. Riders crash into each other on purpose, just for fun.

question_text: What low box with four wheels and a long handle do kids pull around with toys inside?
explanation: A wagon is a low box with four wheels and a long handle. Kids use it to pull around toys or younger siblings.

question_text: Which train travels in tunnels under city streets?
explanation: A subway is a train that travels in tunnels under the ground. People ride it to move quickly around big cities.

question_text: Where does a car stop at home overnight?
explanation: A garage is a small building or room next to a house. It keeps the car safe and dry when no one is driving it.

question_text: Which big metal vehicle has many windows and floats high above Earth?
explanation: A space station is a big lab that floats in space high above Earth. Astronauts live and work inside it for many months.

question_text: What kind of train rides on just a single rail high above the ground?
explanation: A monorail rides on a single rail high above the ground. You see them in zoos and theme parks taking people around.

question_text: Which sled is pulled by a team of strong dogs?
explanation: A dog sled has runners that slide on snow and ice. A team of strong dogs pulls it across frozen lands.

question_text: What slow vehicle was pulled by horses long ago, before there were cars?
explanation: A horse-drawn carriage is a wooden box on wheels. Long ago, before cars were invented, this is how people traveled.

question_text: What is the name for a long, fancy car that people rent for special occasions?
explanation: A limousine is much longer than a regular car. People rent them for special days like weddings or birthdays.

question_text: What special car competes on a track to be the fastest?
explanation: A race car is built to be very light and very fast. Drivers race them around a track to see who finishes first.

question_text: What do drivers look at to see how fast they are going?
explanation: The speedometer is a small gauge on the dashboard. The needle moves to show how fast the car is going right now.

question_text: What do drivers use to look at what is behind them?
explanation: Mirrors let drivers see other cars behind them. Cars have one mirror inside and one on each side.

question_text: What time of day must drivers turn on their headlights?
explanation: At night it is dark outside. Headlights help drivers see the road and help others see their car coming.

question_text: What sign tells drivers a school is nearby and to drive carefully?
explanation: A school zone sign warns drivers that kids may be crossing the road. Drivers must slow down and watch closely.

question_text: What do tanks and bulldozers ride on instead of regular wheels?
explanation: Tanks and bulldozers ride on tracks instead of regular wheels. The tracks spread their weight so they don't sink in mud.

question_text: Which boat carries giant containers full of toys, food, and clothes between countries?
explanation: A cargo ship is huge and full of giant metal boxes. Most things you buy at a store traveled to your country on one.

question_text: What is an airplane without an engine that just glides through the air?
explanation: A glider has wings like a plane but no engine. It rides on air currents the way birds soar.

question_text: What flat board do you ride standing up on top of ocean waves?
explanation: A surfboard is a flat board you ride standing up. Surfers paddle out to sea and stand up as waves push them back to shore.

question_text: What part of a bike do you spin with your feet to make it go?
explanation: Pedals are connected to a chain that turns the back wheel. The faster you push the pedals, the faster the bike goes.

question_text: Which truck carries away kitchen scraps and trash from your house?
explanation: A garbage truck has a big arm or strong workers who lift trash bins and dump them inside. Then it drives the trash to a landfill.

question_text: What sign with a big triangle tells drivers to slow down and let others go first?
explanation: A yield sign is a triangle pointing down. It tells drivers to slow down and let other cars or people go first.

question_text: What special raised path is just for people walking?
explanation: A sidewalk is a flat path right next to the road. People walk safely on it so cars don't hit them.

question_text: Which moving stairway carries people up and down at the airport or mall?
explanation: An escalator is a moving staircase. You step on and it carries you up or down without you having to climb.

question_text: Who built and flew the first powered airplane in 1903?
explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew their plane at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina in 1903. The flight lasted just 12 seconds but changed the world.

question_text: What famous ship sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
explanation: The RMS Titanic was the largest ship of its time. On its very first voyage, it struck an iceberg in the North Atlantic and sank.

question_text: What was the name of the spacecraft that first landed humans on the Moon in 1969?
explanation: Apollo 11 carried Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins to the Moon. Armstrong became the first person to walk on its surface.

question_text: What car company built the famous Model T, the first car that everyday families could afford?
explanation: Henry Ford's company built the Model T starting in 1908. Using a moving assembly line, Ford made cars cheap enough for ordinary people to buy.

question_text: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on July 20, 1969. His famous words were: 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.'

question_text: Who was the first human to travel into space?
explanation: Yuri Gagarin from the Soviet Union orbited Earth on April 12, 1961. He became the very first person to leave our planet.

question_text: What is the curved bottom of a boat called?
explanation: The hull is the main body of a boat — the curved part that touches the water. A strong hull keeps the boat from leaking.

question_text: What is the tall pole on a sailboat that holds the sail called?
explanation: The mast is a tall vertical pole. The sail hangs from it and catches the wind to push the boat forward.

question_text: What is the flat blade under a boat that helps the captain steer?
explanation: The rudder is a flat blade at the back of the boat. Turning it left or right pushes the boat in the opposite direction.

question_text: What is the body of an airplane called?
explanation: The fuselage is the long tube-shaped body of a plane. Passengers, crew, and cargo all ride inside it.

question_text: What is the front of a boat called?
explanation: The bow is the front, pointed end of a boat. It cuts through the water as the boat moves forward.

question_text: What is the back of a boat called?
explanation: The stern is the back of a boat. The rudder and propeller are usually mounted at the stern.

question_text: What is the panel of dials and screens in front of a car driver called?
explanation: The dashboard sits in front of the driver. It holds the speedometer, fuel gauge, warning lights, and music controls.

question_text: Which gauge in a car shows how many miles the car has driven in its lifetime?
explanation: The odometer counts miles. It keeps adding up so you can see the total distance the car has traveled since it was new.

question_text: What pedal do drivers push to make a car go faster?
explanation: The accelerator (gas pedal) is on the right. Pressing it sends more fuel to the engine so the car speeds up.

question_text: What kind of car uses BOTH an electric motor AND a gasoline engine?
explanation: A hybrid car switches between two power sources. It saves fuel by using the electric motor for slow city driving.

question_text: What kind of engine powered the first trains?
explanation: Old trains burned coal to boil water into steam. The steam pushed pistons that turned the wheels.

question_text: Which American invented the moving assembly line that made cars cheap to build?
explanation: Henry Ford's assembly line moved cars past workers. Each worker added one part, which was much faster than building one car at a time.

question_text: Which company makes the Tesla electric car?
explanation: Tesla, started by Elon Musk and others, builds electric cars and trucks. They run on big battery packs instead of gasoline.

question_text: What are Japan's super-fast trains called?
explanation: Japan's Shinkansen is nicknamed the bullet train because of its pointed nose and high speed. They can go over 200 miles per hour.

question_text: Which kind of train floats above its track on powerful magnets?
explanation: A maglev train uses magnetic levitation — magnets push it up off the track. With no friction, it can reach incredible speeds.

question_text: What was the name of the supersonic passenger plane that crossed the Atlantic in just 3 hours?
explanation: The Concorde was a sleek jet that flew faster than the speed of sound. It carried passengers between London, Paris, and New York from 1976 to 2003.

question_text: What kind of small remote-controlled flying vehicle has 4 propellers and is often used to take photos?
explanation: A drone (or quadcopter) has four small propellers. Pilots fly it from the ground using a remote control.

question_text: What is the round window on a ship called?
explanation: A porthole is a small round window on a ship's side. The thick glass and metal frame keep water out even in rough seas.

question_text: What is the room on a ship where the captain steers from called?
explanation: The bridge is the high room with windows on a ship. From here the captain and crew can see in all directions.

question_text: What kind of huge ship has airplanes that take off from its deck?
explanation: An aircraft carrier is a floating airbase. Its long flat deck lets fighter jets take off and land far out at sea.

question_text: What kind of vehicle floats above the water and land on a cushion of air?
explanation: A hovercraft has powerful fans that push air down. The cushion of air lifts it just above the surface so it can travel on water, ice, or land.

question_text: What kind of one-person boat is paddled with a double-bladed paddle?
explanation: A kayak is a small enclosed boat. The paddler uses a paddle with blades on BOTH ends, dipping each side back and forth.

question_text: What kind of sailboat has TWO hulls side by side instead of one?
explanation: A catamaran has two hulls connected by a deck. The wide base makes it very stable and hard to tip over.

question_text: What kind of bridge can be raised to let tall ships pass underneath?
explanation: A drawbridge has a section that tilts up like a door. When a tall boat needs to pass, traffic stops and the bridge opens.

question_text: In which city was the world's first underground railway (subway) built?
explanation: London opened the world's first underground line in 1863. Locals still call their subway 'the Tube' because of its round tunnels.

question_text: What three-wheeled small taxi is found all over Thailand?
explanation: A tuk-tuk has three wheels, an open back, and a small loud engine. The name comes from the noise the engine makes.

question_text: What long, narrow boat with a curved tip is rowed through the canals of Venice?
explanation: A gondola is steered by one person standing up with a single oar. They have carried people through Venice's canals for hundreds of years.

question_text: What two-wheeled passenger vehicle was once pulled by a person running on foot?
explanation: A rickshaw is a small cart with two wheels. In old Asia, a runner pulled passengers from place to place. Today many use bike or motor power.

question_text: What small unmanned spacecraft has NASA sent to drive around on Mars?
explanation: A rover is a robot car that drives on another planet's surface. NASA's rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance explore Mars.

question_text: Which giant rocket carried astronauts from Earth to the Moon during the Apollo missions?
explanation: The Saturn V was the most powerful rocket ever built. It towered 36 stories tall and could lift 130 tons into orbit.

question_text: What spacecraft did NASA use to take astronauts to space from 1981 to 2011?
explanation: The Space Shuttle was the first reusable spacecraft. It took off like a rocket and glided back to Earth like an airplane.

question_text: Which company built the Crew Dragon spacecraft that takes astronauts to the space station today?
explanation: SpaceX, founded by Elon Musk, built the Crew Dragon capsule. It's the first private spacecraft to carry astronauts.

question_text: Which rocket company was started by Jeff Bezos?
explanation: Blue Origin builds rockets for space travel and tourism. Bezos started the company in 2000.

question_text: What gas do most regular cars burn for fuel?
explanation: Gasoline is the most common car fuel. It's made from oil that's pumped out of the ground and refined.

question_text: What fuel do most big trucks and buses use?
explanation: Diesel fuel is heavier than gasoline and gives more power per gallon. That makes it good for hauling heavy loads.

question_text: What kind of slow-moving aircraft is filled with gas that is lighter than air?
explanation: A blimp is a large balloon shaped like a sausage with engines and a small cabin under it. Helium gas inside lets it float.

question_text: What was the name of the famous airship that caught fire and crashed in 1937?
explanation: The Hindenburg was a giant German airship filled with hydrogen. It exploded while landing in New Jersey, ending the age of passenger airships.

question_text: How many wheels does a typical 18-wheeler truck have?
explanation: An 18-wheeler is a truck and trailer combo. The cab and trailer together have 18 wheels — that's where the name comes from.

question_text: What part of a tire grips the road and is made of patterns and grooves?
explanation: The tread is the patterned rubber on the outside of a tire. Its grooves push water out of the way and give the tire grip.

question_text: What bumpy air do pilots call the shaking that planes feel during a flight?
explanation: Turbulence is rough, choppy air. It bounces the plane up and down — which is why pilots ask passengers to wear seat belts.

question_text: What is the cloud-like white trail that planes leave high in the sky?
explanation: A contrail forms when hot exhaust from jet engines meets very cold air high up. The water vapor freezes into a trail of tiny ice crystals.

question_text: What heavy military vehicle has treads, a turret, and fires shells?
explanation: A tank has a thick metal body, treads instead of wheels, and a turret on top with a big cannon. Its armor protects soldiers inside.

question_text: What four-wheeled off-road vehicle has no doors and is often used for riding on dirt trails for fun?
explanation: ATV stands for All-Terrain Vehicle. It's a small open vehicle with knobby tires made to go over rough ground.

question_text: What is the name of the famous American highway system that connects North and South America?
explanation: The Pan-American Highway runs roughly 19,000 miles from Alaska to the southern tip of Argentina. It's the world's longest 'motorable road'.

question_text: What word means a person who walks somewhere instead of driving?
explanation: A pedestrian is anyone traveling on foot. Special crosswalks and sidewalks help keep pedestrians safe from cars.

question_text: What was the name of the first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957?
explanation: Sputnik 1 was about the size of a beach ball. It circled Earth every 96 minutes and started the 'space race' between the US and USSR.

question_text: What was the name of the dog that became the first living being to orbit Earth?
explanation: Laika was a stray dog from Moscow. The Soviet Union sent her into orbit in 1957 aboard Sputnik 2.

question_text: In what year did the Wright Brothers fly the first powered airplane?
explanation: On December 17, 1903, the Wright Flyer lifted off the sand at Kitty Hawk. It flew 120 feet in 12 seconds.

question_text: Which planet have humans sent the most rovers to?
explanation: Mars is the most explored planet besides Earth. NASA, China, and others have landed many rovers there to look for signs of water and life.

question_text: What kind of small motorcycle is built for racing on dirt trails and jumps?
explanation: A dirt bike has knobby tires and high suspension. It's lightweight so riders can launch over jumps and ride through mud.

question_text: What's the name of an airplane with TWO sets of wings stacked on top of each other?
explanation: A biplane has two pairs of wings, one above the other. They were common in the early days of flight, including World War I.

question_text: What's the small spinning blade on the front of many small airplanes called?
explanation: A propeller spins like a giant fan. Its angled blades push air backward, which pulls the plane forward.

question_text: What is the steering wheel of a ship called?
explanation: The helm is the wheel a ship's captain uses to steer. Old ships had wooden wheels with handles sticking out around the edge.

question_text: What is the cargo storage area inside a ship called?
explanation: The hold is the large space below the deck. Crates, containers, and other goods are stored there during the voyage.

question_text: Which side of a boat is called 'port' when you are facing the front?
explanation: Port is the LEFT side of a ship when you face forward. A trick to remember: 'port' and 'left' both have four letters.

question_text: Which side of a boat is called 'starboard' when you are facing the front?
explanation: Starboard is the RIGHT side of a ship when you face forward. The word comes from the old steering oar that was on the right side.

question_text: What was the name of the famous plane Charles Lindbergh flew solo across the Atlantic in 1927?
explanation: Lindbergh flew the Spirit of St. Louis from New York to Paris — 33 hours nonstop, all alone. He became the first person to do it.

question_text: Which famous female pilot was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean?
explanation: Amelia Earhart made her solo Atlantic flight in 1932. She set many records before disappearing during a flight around the world in 1937.

question_text: What kind of small fast plane fights other planes in the air?
explanation: Fighter jets are sleek, single-pilot planes built for speed and quick turning. Modern ones can fly faster than the speed of sound.

question_text: What kind of vehicle drives on land AND swims through water?
explanation: An amphibious vehicle has wheels for land and a watertight body for water. The military uses them to carry soldiers from ships onto beaches.

question_text: What is a small two-wheeled vehicle with a small motor and a step-through frame called?
explanation: A moped is a small motorbike with a low engine. Riders can sit upright with feet flat on the deck.

question_text: What kind of large electric streetcar runs on rails through city streets?
explanation: A tram (or streetcar) rides on rails set into the road. It gets power from a wire above the track.

question_text: What hangs under a wire and is famous in San Francisco for climbing steep hills?
explanation: San Francisco's cable cars grip a moving cable buried under the street. The cable pulls the cars up the city's famous steep hills.

question_text: In which country do drivers usually drive on the LEFT side of the road?
explanation: The UK drives on the left, along with Australia, Japan, India, and several others. Most of the world drives on the right.

question_text: What does a yellow traffic light mean?
options: Slow down — light will turn red
explanation: Yellow warns drivers the light is about to turn red. Drivers should slow down and stop if they can do so safely.

question_text: What kind of plane drops water on forest fires?
explanation: A water bomber scoops water from lakes or fills its tanks at airports. Then it dumps the water from low altitude onto burning trees.

question_text: What chimpanzee did NASA send into space in 1961, before the first US astronaut?
explanation: Ham was a young chimp from Cameroon. His test flight proved a primate could survive launch and weightlessness, paving the way for human flights.

question_text: What ancient wheeled vehicle was pulled by horses and used for racing or war in old Greece and Rome?
explanation: A chariot was a small two-wheeled platform pulled by horses. Drivers stood up to race them or fight in battle.

question_text: What flying machine, made by the Montgolfier brothers in 1783, was the first to lift people into the air?
explanation: The Montgolfier brothers' hot air balloon used a fire to heat air inside a fabric balloon. Hot air rises, so the balloon lifted off.

question_text: What lane on a road is reserved for people riding bikes?
explanation: A bike lane is a marked strip on the road for cyclists. It keeps bikes separate from cars so everyone is safer.

question_text: What does ABS stand for in cars?
explanation: ABS = Anti-lock Braking System. It pumps the brakes very quickly to keep the wheels from locking up, so the driver can still steer during a hard stop.

question_text: What is the long thin tube on a submarine that lets sailors see above the water?
explanation: A periscope uses mirrors to bend light. Sailors deep below can look through the eyepiece and see what's happening on the surface.

question_text: What is the long metal beam that connects a car's pair of wheels called?
explanation: An axle is a strong metal rod that runs between two wheels. The wheels spin around the axle as the car moves.

question_text: What pedal does a driver press to slow down or stop a car?
explanation: The brake pedal is to the left of the accelerator. Pressing it squeezes pads against the wheels to slow the car down.

question_text: What part of a car helps absorb bumps for a smoother ride?
explanation: The suspension is a system of springs and shock absorbers between the wheels and the body. It softens bumps so passengers don't feel every pothole.

question_text: What underwater vessel can dive deep, hide for months, and is used by navies?
explanation: A submarine is a long tube-shaped vessel built to travel underwater. Modern military submarines can stay submerged for many months.

question_text: What is the rotating piece on top of a tank that holds the cannon called?
explanation: A turret is the dome on top of a tank that can spin all the way around. It lets the crew aim the cannon in any direction.

question_text: Which country invented the modern bullet train (Shinkansen)?
explanation: Japan opened the first bullet train line in 1964, in time for the Tokyo Olympics. It connected Tokyo and Osaka at speeds over 130 mph.

question_text: What is the world's longest railway line, crossing all of Russia?
explanation: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs over 5,700 miles from Moscow to Vladivostok. The full trip takes about a week.

question_text: What is the name for the entire system of buses, trains, and subways in a city?
explanation: Public transportation is run by cities for everyone to share. It moves many people while taking up much less space than private cars.

question_text: What kind of helmet must motorcycle riders wear by law in most places?
explanation: A motorcycle helmet covers the whole head, including a face shield. It is built to protect the rider in a high-speed crash.

question_text: What does a flashing red light at a railroad crossing mean?
options: Train is coming — stop and wait
explanation: Flashing red lights and the bell warn drivers a train is approaching. Cars must stop before the tracks until the lights turn off.

question_text: What boat carries cars and people across rivers and bays on short trips?
explanation: A ferry is a flat-decked boat that runs the same route over and over. People drive their cars on at one side and off at the other.

question_text: What strong rope is used to tie a boat to a dock?
explanation: A mooring line is a thick rope. Sailors tie one end to the boat and the other to a dock cleat to keep the boat in place.

question_text: What do helicopters use for landing instead of wheels?
explanation: Most helicopters have skids — long metal tubes — instead of wheels. Skids are lighter and let the helicopter land almost anywhere.

question_text: What is the part of a wheel that holds the spokes together in the middle?
explanation: The hub is the center of a wheel. Spokes connect the hub to the rim, like rays going out from the center.

question_text: What pedal is between the brake and accelerator in a manual-shift car?
explanation: The clutch lets the driver change gears smoothly. Pressing it disconnects the engine from the wheels for just a moment.

question_text: What heavy ship-pulling truck of the road has 18 wheels and drives long distances?
explanation: A semi-trailer truck (semi) hauls a separate cargo trailer. The combined cab and trailer have 18 wheels, which is why it's called an 18-wheeler.

question_text: What is the world's busiest airport, with the most passengers each year?
explanation: Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson airport has been one of the world's busiest for many years. It serves more than 100 million passengers a year.

question_text: Which famous animal once carried Spanish explorers across deserts because it stores water in its body?
explanation: Camels can survive long stretches without water. They were the most important transport across deserts in Africa, Arabia, and Asia for thousands of years.

question_text: In Asia, which large strong animal was used for hundreds of years to carry people and heavy loads?
explanation: Elephants were used for transport, logging, and ceremonies in India, Thailand, and other Asian countries. They can carry hundreds of pounds.

question_text: What was the largest cargo airplane ever built, used by Ukraine to carry huge loads?
explanation: The Antonov An-225 'Mriya' was a six-engine giant. Only one was ever built, and it could carry 250 tons of cargo.

question_text: Which Boeing jumbo jet has a hump on top and was once the world's most famous passenger plane?
explanation: The Boeing 747 first flew in 1969. Its second deck (the hump) made it instantly recognizable in airports for over 50 years.

question_text: What is the largest passenger plane in the world, made by Airbus, with two full decks?
explanation: The Airbus A380 has two full decks running the length of the plane. It can carry over 500 passengers.

question_text: What kind of small plane sprays insecticide or fertilizer over farm fields?
explanation: A crop duster is a small low-flying plane. It sprays liquid over crops to keep bugs away or help plants grow.

question_text: What kind of plane lands on water using floats instead of wheels?
explanation: A sea plane (or float plane) has long pontoons under it instead of landing gear. It can take off and land on lakes and harbors.

question_text: What underwater vessel set the record by reaching the deepest point in the ocean (Mariana Trench) in 1960?
explanation: The Trieste was a special deep-diving submersible. It carried two people nearly seven miles down to the bottom of the Pacific Ocean.

question_text: What is the long air-filled tube on a fire truck used to spray water?
explanation: A fire hose is a long flexible tube. Firefighters connect it to a fire hydrant or the truck's tank to blast water at the flames.

question_text: What's the round opening on the side of a ship sometimes called?
explanation: A porthole is a small round window in a ship's hull or cabin. Its thick glass keeps water out even when waves splash against it.

question_text: What kind of small high-speed boat lifts itself out of the water on underwater wings?
explanation: A hydrofoil has small wing-like blades under the hull. As it speeds up, the blades lift the boat out of the water for less drag.

question_text: Which colorful taxi-bus, often decorated with bright art, is famous in the Philippines?
explanation: Jeepneys started as old US Army jeeps after World War II. Drivers extended them to carry many passengers and painted them with colorful art.

question_text: What is the name for the part of a sailboat that holds the bottom of the sail and swings side to side?
explanation: The boom is the horizontal pole at the bottom of the sail. Sailors duck when it swings across the boat (called 'jibing').

question_text: What very long road famously stretches from Chicago to Los Angeles in the United States?
explanation: Route 66 was one of the first US highways. Its 2,400 miles became famous in songs, books, and movies as the 'Mother Road'.

question_text: What kind of bridge hangs from huge cables strung between tall towers, like the Golden Gate Bridge?
explanation: A suspension bridge uses thick cables to hold up the road deck. The cables transfer weight to tall towers at each end.

question_text: What kind of small electric two-wheel vehicle is shared in many cities and rented through an app?
explanation: E-scooters have a small electric motor and a rechargeable battery. Riders unlock them with a phone app and pay for the time used.

question_text: What kind of train station-to-station ride do many people use to go to work each day?
explanation: A commute is the regular trip a person takes from home to work and back. Many commuters take trains, buses, or subways.

question_text: What part of a car covers and protects the engine?
explanation: The hood (called the bonnet in the UK) is the metal panel at the front of a car. Lift it up and you'll see the engine inside.

question_text: What is the small wheel-like control inside a plane that pilots use to steer?
explanation: The yoke is the steering control in front of the pilot. Pulling it back makes the plane climb; pushing it forward makes it descend.

question_text: What lever does a pilot push forward to give the engines more power?
explanation: The throttle controls how much fuel the engines burn. Push it forward for more thrust; pull it back to slow down.

question_text: What kind of small wheeled vehicle does a baby ride in while a grown-up jogs?
explanation: A jogging stroller has three large air-filled tires for a smooth ride at jogging speed. It's built to handle bumps better than a regular stroller.

question_text: Which space telescope, named after a famous astronomer, has taken amazing pictures of distant galaxies since 1990?
explanation: The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth above the blurry atmosphere. It's named for Edwin Hubble, who first proved galaxies exist beyond our own.

question_text: What heavy machine on a building site flattens fresh asphalt to make a smooth road?
explanation: A road roller has huge smooth metal drums for wheels. Driving back and forth packs down the asphalt and flattens the road surface.

question_text: What construction machine has a digging arm at one end and a loader bucket at the other?
explanation: A backhoe loader is a tractor with two attachments: a small digger arm at the back and a wide loader bucket at the front.

question_text: What machine carries pallets of boxes around warehouses by lifting them with two metal forks?
explanation: A forklift has two metal blades (forks) that slide under a pallet. Hydraulic lifts raise the pallet so a worker can move heavy stacks.

question_text: What were the first electric self-balancing two-wheelers that you stand on, popular in the 2000s?
explanation: The Segway has two wheels side by side and a tall handle. Sensors keep it upright as the rider leans forward and back.

question_text: What is the name for a hot-air-balloon flight that's open to passengers?
explanation: A balloon ride takes passengers high above the ground in a big wicker basket below the balloon. The pilot uses a propane burner to control altitude.

question_text: What kind of fast military boat is small, heavily armed, and used to attack other ships?
explanation: A patrol boat is a small fast warship. Navies use them to guard coasts and chase down smugglers or enemy boats.

question_text: What kind of tall lookout post on an old sailing ship sits on top of the mast?
explanation: The crow's nest was a small platform high on the mast. A sailor stood there to spot land, ships, or danger far away.

question_text: What is the name of NASA's huge new rocket built to carry astronauts back to the Moon?
explanation: The Space Launch System (SLS) is NASA's most powerful rocket since Saturn V. It launched the uncrewed Artemis I mission around the Moon in 2022.
